summary: Longest subarray with an equal number of 0s and 1s.
mainInsight: Map 0 to -1 so that a balanced subarray has sum 0. With a running sum, two equal prefix sums mean the elements between them sum to 0. Store the first index of each prefix sum (with {0: -1}) and take the longest distance.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.summary: Count zeros and ones for every subarray.

approaches.name: Prefix sum + first occurrence map
approaches.summary: Convert 0 to -1; look up the earliest index of the same sum.

commonMistakes: Overwriting the first index of a prefix sum

promptVariants: What trick turns 'equal zeros and ones' into a sum problem?
How do you detect a balanced subarray with a running total?
options: Treat 0 as -1, so a balanced subarray has total 0 (repeated prefix sum)
Treat 1 as -1, so a balanced subarray has a total of 1
Sort the array, so that equal counts become neighbours
Count only the ones, since the zeros are then implied
cards.answer: Treat 0 as -1, so a balanced subarray has total 0 (repeated prefix sum)
cards.explanation: Equal prefix sums at i and j mean the elements in (i, j] sum to 0.

promptVariants: Why store only the first index of each prefix sum, and why seed the map with {0: -1}?
cards.answer: The longest subarray ending at j for a given prefix sum starts after the earliest index with that sum, so only the first occurrence is kept. The seed {0: -1} represents the empty prefix, so a balanced subarray that starts at index 0 is measured correctly.
keyPoints: First occurrence gives the longest span
cards.explanation: Do not overwrite the stored index.
One pass with O(1) map operations.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
cards.explanation: The map can hold up to n distinct prefix sums.

options: 3: the whole array has equal counts
cards.explanation: Prefix sums are -1, 0, -1; the repeat of -1 at index 2 gives length 2.

incorrectOptionExplanations.3: the whole array has equal counts: It has two zeros and one one.
incorrectOptionExplanations.1: only single elements are balanced: A single element is never balanced.
